recognize_zh: 試管內紅血球懸浮液中可見大量肉眼可見的細小紅色顆粒狀凝集塊（agglutinates），而非均勻的紅色懸浮液，符合冷凝集素（cold agglutinin）試驗陽性。
features: Test tube containing a red cell suspension viewed grossly
Numerous fine, speckled red agglutinates dispersed throughout the fluid and along the glass wall
Suspending medium between clumps is only lightly tinged rather than uniformly opaque red
No single compact button; clumping is granular and diffuse
Temperature of incubation and reversibility on warming cannot be assessed from the photograph
describe_en: Gross photograph of a test tube containing a red cell suspension shows numerous fine, macroscopically visible red cell agglutinates distributed throughout the fluid and adherent to the tube wall, in contrast to a homogeneous suspension. The image alone does not document the incubation temperature, titer, or reversal of agglutination on warming to 37 °C. In the appropriate setting (cold-incubated sample with dispersal on warming, DAT positive for C3d), findings are consistent with a positive cold agglutinin test, supporting cold agglutinin disease.

ddx.vs: Rouleaux form stacked coin-like aggregates that disperse on saline replacement, whereas true agglutinates persist in saline and disperse only on warming in CAD.
Warm autoantibodies rarely cause gross agglutination; agglutination does not reverse at 37 °C and the DAT is typically IgG positive rather than C3d only.
The Donath-Landsteiner IgG biphasic hemolysin causes hemolysis rather than prominent agglutination and is confirmed by the Donath-Landsteiner test.
Low-titer, narrow thermal-amplitude cold agglutinins may clump cells at 4 °C but not near body temperature; titer and thermal amplitude separate them.
